newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More shipping firms merging to cope in tough times.
newsitem.headline: More shipping firms merging to cope in tough times.

text.p: More shipping firms are merging to cope with tough times and the trend is likely to continue, industry experts said on Monday.

"The familiar institutions of conferences and consortia in international shipping appear less able to cope with the changes and the industry must seek new co-operative arranges for its long term viability," said Lua Cheng Eng, President of the Singapore National Shipping Assosiation.

"The recently announced P&O/Nedlloyd and the NOL/APL mergers are example of the new initiatives of the industry in further rationalising itself," he told the sixth Asian Shipowners Forum. Two big European shipping firms, P&O and Nedlloyd, have merged recently.
Singapore's Neptune Orient Lines has acquired American carrier APL Ltd and Hanjin Shipping has become the majority shareholder in German shipping firm DSR-Senator Lines.
Sumate Tanthwanit, Chairman of the Asian Shipowners Forum, said shipowners faced extremely difficult operating and technical conditions in a declining freight market.
"Some shipowners have succumbed in the wake of all these difficult conditions whilst others have decided to rationalise to survive," he said.
Industry experts at the conference said Asian shipowners were expected to operate over half of the world fleet by 2000, riding on rapidly developing Asia Pacific economies.

According to the Economic and Social commissions for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), regional economies will continue grow strongly between five and seven percent annually in the 20 years to 2015, Sumate said.
Asian shipowners now control more than 40 percent of the world merchant fleet and this percentage would grow, he said.
